analysis.investment_thesis: Cyient is the most reasonably valued stock in this group — FCF yield of ~6.5% (INR 688 Cr / INR 10,625 Cr) is at the low end of acceptable, EV/EBITDA of 13.6x is undemanding for a diversified engineering services firm, and the balance sheet is clean. The concern is that FY25 saw earnings and EBITDA decline versus FY24, suggesting the growth story has hit turbulence just as consensus is extrapolating prior-year peaks.
key_strengths: FCF yield of ~6.5% and consistent positive OCF (5/5 years) provide a real earnings floor and downside protection
Near-zero leverage (D/E 0.07) with INR 1,067 Cr cash on balance sheet gives financial flexibility; net debt is effectively negative
Diversified end-market exposure (aerospace, rail, utilities, semiconductor) reduces single-cycle concentration risk
key_risks: FY25 net profit of INR 648 Cr and EBITDA of INR 1,224 Cr are both DOWN from FY24 peaks of INR 703 Cr and INR 1,376 Cr — earnings contraction in an ostensibly growing company is a serious warning signal
Low promoter stake of 23.28% is well below peers — limited skin in the game and potential governance overhang
Finance cost CAGR of 21.6% over 9 years (from INR 16 Cr to INR 93 Cr) reflects increasing capital consumption even as other income contracts
red_flags: Other income declined from INR 140 Cr (FY21) to nearly zero (FY24) — prior earnings quality was partly supported by non-operating gains that have now disappeared
Operating margin of 9% is thin and declining; the FY24-25 compression raises questions about pricing power and offshore delivery leverage
Engineering services is not a high-moat business — client concentration and global sourcing alternatives limit pricing power
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Cyient passes my first filter — FCF yield above 6% means I am not paying purely for hope. The balance sheet is clean, the business has grown revenue at 10% CAGR over nine years, and the forward PE of 14.6x is not demanding. This is the kind of unglamorous name that tends to get overlooked in a bull market obsessed with defense and capital goods, which is precisely where I look for value.

However, the FY25 earnings decline is the key ambiguity. If FY24 was the peak and margins are structurally compressing in engineering services (wage inflation, client-side insourcing), then the forward PE of 14.6x is not as cheap as it looks. The falling other income also means prior EPS was somewhat flattering. I would characterize Cyient as fairly valued to modestly undervalued — a hold with potential to become a buy on further weakness toward INR 800-850, where FCF yield improves to 7.5-8%.
